sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe the benefits of using cloud services

questions.stem: A toy retailer expects its web traffic to surge during a product launch and then return to normal. Which cloud benefit directly addresses adding and removing capacity as demand changes?
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the cloud benefit that matches automatic capacity adjustment. It is different from reliability, which focuses on surviving failures.

options.explanation: Elasticity scales resources out or in as demand rises or falls.
Reliability helps a workload continue through failures, not primarily adjust to demand spikes.
Governance applies rules and standards; it does not describe capacity scaling.
A SaaS offering is a ready-to-use application model; it does not name the benefit of scaling capacity up or down.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe the benefits of using cloud services

questions.stem: Which **two** actions are examples of governance for Azure resources?
questions.explanation: Governance applies organizational rules and metadata. Policy can enforce allowed settings, and tags can identify ownership or cost allocation.

options.text: Require an Owner tag on resource groups
options.explanation: Required tags improve ownership, organization, and reporting.

options.text: Deny deployments in unapproved regions with Azure Policy
options.explanation: Azure Policy can enforce allowed locations.

options.text: Use archive tier for a frequently edited document library
options.explanation: Archive tier is a storage access choice and is unsuitable for frequently edited data.

options.text: Peer two virtual networks for private connectivity
options.explanation: VNet peering is networking, not a governance standard.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe the benefits of using cloud services

questions.stem: True or false: Cloud predictability can be improved by monitoring workload behavior and testing changes before production rollout.
questions.explanation: The statement is true because predictability is about reducing surprises through known behavior, measured trends, and controlled changes.

options.explanation: Correct. Monitoring trends and testing changes before release reduce surprises and make workload behavior more predictable.
Choosing False misses that predictability comes from measured behavior, validation, and controlled production changes.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe the benefits of using cloud services

questions.stem: Match each cloud operations request to the concept it most directly represents.
questions.explanation: The requests point to distinct concepts: elasticity for changing capacity, governance for rules, reliability for failure tolerance, and manageability for operational tooling.

prompts.text: Automatically add instances during a flash sale
Block deployments that lack required business tags
Continue serving users if a component fails
Use alerts and automation runbooks for daily operations

explanations.p2: Governance enforces organizational standards such as required tags.
explanations.p3: Reliability focuses on continuity during failures.
explanations.p4: Manageability uses monitoring, automation, and management tools.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe Cloud Service Types

questions.stem: Put the steps in order for moving a legacy web app to the most appropriate cloud service model.
questions.explanation: A realistic service-model decision starts by identifying constraints, then selecting the model, then assigning responsibilities for the chosen model, and finally validating operations after migration.

items.text: List requirements for guest OS control, custom code, identity, and data handling
Choose IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS based on the required control and management tradeoff
Assign customer-owned tasks such as data classification, access, and app configuration
Test monitoring, backup, and update procedures for the selected model

explanations.s1: Requirements must be understood before a service model can be selected.
explanations.s2: The model choice follows the control and management requirements.
explanations.s3: Shared responsibilities are clarified after the model is chosen.
explanations.s4: Operational procedures are validated once responsibilities and design are known.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe Cloud Service Types

questions.stem: Classify each scenario by the cloud service model it best represents.
questions.explanation: IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS differ by how much the customer manages versus how much the provider manages.

items.text: A VM where the customer installs middleware and patches the guest OS
items.explanation: Customer guest OS and middleware administration are IaaS characteristics.

items.text: A managed web app platform for deploying custom application code
items.explanation: PaaS supports custom code while reducing OS and platform maintenance.

items.text: A provider-managed accounting application used through a browser
items.explanation: A finished provider-managed application consumed by users is SaaS.

items.text: A lift-and-shift database server that requires OS-level backup software
items.explanation: OS-level software requirements point to IaaS VM control.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe Cloud Service Types

questions.stem: Complete the sentence about a cloud service model for custom applications.
questions.explanation: PaaS is the model that lets developers deploy custom applications while the provider handles more of the operating system and platform maintenance.

fillInBlank.template: When a team deploys custom application code but wants Azure to manage the operating system and application platform, the service model is {{b1}}.

blanks.explanation: PaaS is the accepted model for custom code with managed platform responsibilities.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe Cloud Service Types

questions.scenario: Fabrikam is choosing between hosting a custom app on VMs, deploying it to a managed web platform, or subscribing to a finished business application.
questions.stem: For each statement about the service models, select **Yes** if it is true. Otherwise, select **No**.
questions.explanation: The statements test how responsibility changes across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS while customer control decreases from IaaS toward SaaS.

statements.text: IaaS usually provides more guest operating system control than PaaS.
statements.explanation: IaaS exposes VM-level control including the guest OS.

statements.text: PaaS is appropriate when developers deploy custom code but want reduced platform maintenance.
statements.explanation: PaaS shifts more platform operation to the provider while keeping custom-code deployment.

statements.text: With SaaS, the customer typically manages the provider's application source code.
statements.explanation: The provider manages the SaaS application; customers manage users, data, and configuration.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe Azure Compute Services

questions.scenario: A VM-based web tier handles seasonal promotions. All instances use the same image, and the operations team wants Azure to add or remove VM instances as load changes.
questions.stem: Which Azure compute feature best matches this requirement?
questions.explanation: Virtual Machine Scale Sets are intended for groups of similar VMs that scale together, which matches the VM-based seasonal web tier.

options.explanation: Scale sets manage and scale identical VM instances as a group.
Contractor desktop delivery is an Azure Virtual Desktop scenario, not scaling a VM web tier.
Azure DNS resolves names and does not add VM instances.
A private endpoint provides private access to a service; it does not scale VMs.

sources.title: az group

questions.stem: A team needs an empty Azure resource group called `rg-compute-prod` in the `eastus` region before deploying compute resources. Which Azure CLI command creates it?
questions.explanation: The command must use the Azure CLI resource-group creation verb with the requested resource group name and target Azure location.

options.explanation: This is the resource group creation command and it supplies eastus as the Azure location for the new container.
A virtual machine scale set command expects an existing resource group and cannot create the container first.

options.text: `az network vnet peering create --name rg-compute-prod --location eastus`
options.explanation: VNet peering commands connect virtual networks; they do not create a resource group.
This would create a storage account in an existing resource group and does not create the resource group itself.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe Azure Compute Services

questions.stem: A photo-processing app must resize an image whenever a blob is added to storage. The team wants to run only the small processing task and avoid managing servers. Which service should it choose?
questions.explanation: Azure Functions is the best choice for small event-driven code triggered by storage events with minimal server administration.

options.explanation: Functions can run code in response to blob events without direct server management.
Desktop virtualization serves interactive user sessions; it would not be chosen to process storage events.
ExpressRoute is a networking connectivity service, so it would not execute an image-resize task.
GRS replicates data to another region; it does not run image-resize code.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe Azure Compute Services

questions.stem: Which **two** Azure features provide private or hybrid network connectivity rather than application hosting?
questions.explanation: VNet peering and VPN Gateway are networking features. They connect networks; they do not host application code.

options.explanation: VNet peering connects Azure VNets privately.
VPN Gateway supports encrypted VPN connectivity such as site-to-site links.
App Service is an application hosting platform, so it is outside the requested connectivity features.
Functions runs event-driven code and is not a network connectivity service.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe Azure Compute Services

questions.stem: True or false: Azure DNS can host DNS zones, while VPN Gateway is used for VPN tunnel connectivity.
questions.explanation: The statement is true because the services solve different networking problems: name resolution versus encrypted network connectivity.

options.explanation: Correct. Azure DNS hosts DNS zones and records, while VPN Gateway provides encrypted VPN connectivity.
Choosing False misses that DNS hosting and VPN tunnel connectivity are separate Azure networking functions.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals

questions.stem: Match each Azure requirement to the service or feature that satisfies it.
questions.explanation: The matches distinguish compute hosting from networking and storage resilience features.

prompts.text: Host a managed web API without managing web servers
Create a private connection from an on-premises site to Azure over VPN
Replicate storage data to a secondary region

explanations.p1: App Service hosts web apps and APIs with managed platform operation.
explanations.p2: Azure Virtual Desktop provides hosted desktops and remote apps.
explanations.p3: VPN Gateway provides VPN tunnel connectivity.
explanations.p4: Geo-redundant storage copies data to a secondary Azure region.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Describe Azure Compute Services

questions.stem: Put the steps in order for selecting a hosting option for a new containerized API.
questions.explanation: The decision should start with application requirements, then determine whether Kubernetes is needed, then choose the managed hosting option, and finally configure network and monitoring needs.

items.text: Confirm runtime needs, traffic pattern, and whether the app is packaged as a container
Decide whether the team needs Kubernetes orchestration or a simpler managed container platform
Select AKS for Kubernetes needs or Container Apps/ACI for simpler managed container scenarios
Configure ingress, scaling rules, and monitoring for the chosen service

explanations.s1: Requirements and packaging are gathered before comparing services.
explanations.s2: The Kubernetes requirement is a key branching decision for container hosting.
explanations.s3: The service is selected after the orchestration need is known.
explanations.s4: Operational settings are configured after the hosting choice is made.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Data redundancy - Azure Storage

questions.stem: Classify each Azure Storage choice by whether it is a redundancy option or a blob access tier.
questions.explanation: Redundancy options describe copy placement for resilience. Access tiers describe expected read patterns and retrieval tradeoffs for blob data.

items.text: Locally redundant storage (LRS)
items.explanation: LRS is a redundancy option that keeps copies within one region location.

items.text: Zone-redundant storage (ZRS)
items.explanation: ZRS is a redundancy option across availability zones in a region.

items.text: Hot
items.explanation: Hot is an access tier for frequently accessed blobs.

items.text: Archive
items.explanation: Archive is an access tier for rarely accessed blobs that can tolerate retrieval steps.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Data redundancy - Azure Storage

questions.stem: Complete the sentence about storing rarely retrieved blob data.
questions.explanation: Archive is the blob access tier intended for data that is rarely accessed and can tolerate retrieval processing before use.

fillInBlank.template: For blob data that is rarely read and can wait for retrieval processing, the lowest-access long-term tier is usually {{b1}}.

blanks.explanation: Archive tier matches rarely accessed blob data that can tolerate retrieval steps.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Data redundancy - Azure Storage

questions.scenario: Woodgrove Bank is designing storage for transaction exports, audit evidence, and a regional recovery requirement.
questions.stem: For each Azure Storage statement, select **Yes** if it is true. Otherwise, select **No**.
questions.explanation: The statements check the difference between redundancy and access tier choices in storage design.

statements.text: GRS can be selected when data must be copied to a secondary Azure region.
statements.explanation: Geo-redundant storage replicates data to another region.

statements.text: Hot tier is intended for blobs that are accessed frequently.
statements.explanation: Hot tier is optimized for frequent access patterns.

statements.text: Archive tier is the best tier for data that must be read immediately many times each hour.
statements.explanation: Frequently and immediately accessed data is a hot-tier scenario, not archive.

sources.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-900: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
Data redundancy - Azure Storage

questions.scenario: A legal team stores compliance documents for years. After the first few weeks, the files are rarely retrieved, and the team can wait while a file is made available before reading it.
questions.stem: Which blob tier should the legal team choose for these rarely retrieved long-term files?
questions.explanation: Because the files are rarely read and the team can wait for retrieval processing, Archive is the best blob access tier for the long-term pattern.

options.explanation: Archive fits long-term, rarely accessed data that can tolerate retrieval delay.
Hot is for frequently accessed data.
VNet peering is networking and has no role in blob access tier selection.
Functions runs code and does not define how blob data is tiered.

questions.stem: During monthly cost cleanup, finance asks operations to create a separate `rg-cost-review` container in West US so resources for a budget analysis can be grouped before tags and budgets are applied. Which Azure CLI command should operations run first?

Defender for Cloud assesses security posture and regulatory compliance recommendations.
Hosted desktops do not evaluate compliance rules or security posture for Azure resources.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order for safely deploying repeatable Azure infrastructure with infrastructure as code.
questions.explanation: A practical IaC workflow defines the desired state, stores and reviews it, deploys with an Azure tool, and then verifies the deployed resources.

items.text: Describe the target resources and settings in a Bicep, ARM, or Terraform file
Review and version the file so changes are tracked before deployment
Run the deployment command or pipeline against the intended Azure scope
Validate that the deployed resources match the approved definition

explanations.s1: The desired state must be written before it can be reviewed or deployed.
explanations.s2: Versioning and review reduce risk before execution.
explanations.s3: Deployment occurs after the approved definition exists.
explanations.s4: Validation confirms the actual environment matches the intended configuration.

items.explanation: Bicep files represent infrastructure as code definitions.
